name: Crossing Graphs Detect and Recover Vertex and Edge Separators
statement: For an irredundant partial cube $H\subseteq Q_F$ with $|F|\ge3$, $H$ has a cut vertex exactly when its crossing graph is disconnected. If $H$ is two-connected, separating edges of direction $e$ are exactly the full fibers over cut vertices of the contraction $\pi_eH$, and such an edge exists exactly when deleting $e$ disconnects the crossing graph. If that deletion has exactly two components $F_1,F_2$, there is exactly one separating $e$-edge; adjoining it to the two components of its complement yields convex coordinate restrictions with exclusive blocks $F_1,F_2$. Consequently an ample pc-minimal obstruction has neither a cut vertex nor a separating edge exactly when its crossing graph is two-connected.
proof: The cut-vertex/crossing-graph theorem applies to $H$ and its contraction, whose crossing graph is obtained by deleting $e$. Fibers of the contraction are connected singletons or $e$-edges, every projected edge lifts, and this remains true after deleting one fiber; hence complement components correspond. Two-connectedness rules out a singleton cut fiber, proving the edge characterization. Crossing-graph components are the coordinate sets of graph blocks: blocks are convex, a coordinate cannot occur in two blocks, and coordinates in distinct blocks do not cross. Two crossing components after deleting $e$ therefore give two quotient blocks at one cut vertex and lift to one separating edge with the claimed convex pieces.
